facility_roles.note: Beam-dump facility fed by the SPS proton beam.

intervals.label: Expression of Interest
intervals.note: The document dated 8 October 2013 is the SPSC Expression of Interest (SPSC-EOI-010); the SHiP Technical Proposal (arXiv:1504.04956, section 1.1) calls it 'the SHiP Expression of Interest'. The EoI text itself is titled 'Proposal to Search for Heavy Neutral Leptons at the SPS' and does not use the name SHiP.
intervals.quote: CERN-SPSC-2013-024 / SPSC-EOI-010 October 8, 2013 Proposal to Search for Heavy Neutral Leptons at the SPS

intervals.label: SPSC review of Technical and Physics Proposal
intervals.note: The only source is CERN Courier, a secondary source, so this is recorded as approximate rather than verified.
intervals.quote: The CERN SPS and PS experiments Committee (SPSC) has recently completed a review of the SHiP Technical and Physics Proposal, and it recommended that the SHiP collaboration proceed towards preparing a Comprehensive Design Report.

intervals.label: approved for ECN3
intervals.note: arXiv:2606.11039 ('The SHiP/NA67 experiment at the ECN3 high-intensity beam facility at the CERN SPS', SHiP Collaboration, submitted 9 June 2026) states verbatim in its abstract that SHiP/BDF was 'approved in 2024' for the ECN3 hall, matching the CERN Research Board's 2024 decision reported by CERN Courier ('SHiP to chart hidden sector', published 3 May 2024, which also names the collaboration's then-current schedule aim of commissioning the facility toward the end of 2030 and the detector in 2031 -- an earlier schedule than the 2033 experiment start recorded in the 'planned experiment start' interval below).

intervals.label: planned experiment start
intervals.locator: arXiv:2606.11039 (PDF), closing paragraph before the acknowledgements
intervals.note: Planned date stated in the SHiP Collaboration's 2026 proceedings (arXiv:2606.11039), which also say the BDF is foreseen to be commissioned with beam by 2033. Recorded as approximate because the schedule is still moving: a May 2024 CERN Courier interview gave an earlier aim (facility towards the end of 2030, detector in 2031).
intervals.quote: Approved in 2024 and to be built within the coming years at the CERN SPS, it will begin data taking in 2033.

name: SHiP
notes: Placed at site:cern-ecn3-north-area, shared with the NA48 and NA62 records; the official site's own description ('High-Intensity ECN3 Facility') supports this placement.

The 2033 planned start is the date stated in a 2026 SHiP Collaboration conference paper (arXiv:2606.11039) and is recorded as approximate because the schedule is still moving (a 2024 CERN Courier interview gave an earlier aim: facility towards the end of 2030, detector in 2031); an official CERN Council or SPSC document would settle it.
No collaboration membership counts found on the official site.

The 2024 CERN Research Board approval of SHiP/BDF for ECN3 is corroborated by arXiv:2606.11039 ('approved in 2024'), so the 'approved for ECN3' interval is recorded as verified. A 3 May 2024 CERN Courier article ('SHiP to chart hidden sector') quotes the collaboration aiming to commission the facility by the end of 2030 and the detector in 2031, earlier than the 2033 planned start, so the year of first physics data is not settled. Two further sources (arXiv:2504.06692 and the abstract of arXiv:2606.11039) show the programme is still called 'SHiP/NA67' in at least one 2026 collaboration paper; this is not added as an alias because the official ship.web.cern.ch site uses only 'SHiP'.

physics_goals.value: Search for feebly interacting long-lived particles beyond the Standard Model -- heavy neutral leptons, dark photons, dark scalars and axion-like particles -- and for light dark matter, using a high-intensity beam-dump facility

physics_goals.quote: ideally suited to study the interactions of tau neutrinos

summary.plain: SHiP is a planned CERN experiment that will dump an intense proton beam into a heavy target and search the debris for new, weakly interacting particles that could explain dark matter and other mysteries. It is approved to be built in the same underground hall once used by NA48 and NA62.
summary.technical: Approved beam-dump experiment for feebly interacting long-lived particles (heavy neutral leptons, dark photons, dark scalars, axion-like particles) and light dark matter, sited at CERN's ECN3 cavern on the SPS. SPSC reviewed the Technical and Physics Proposal in February 2016; approved for ECN3 in 2024 (SHiP Collaboration, 2026); planned experiment start around 2033.

unique_capabilities.value: A dedicated high-intensity beam-dump facility (rather than a collider-detector) designed to maximise sensitivity to hidden-sector particles produced in proton interactions on a heavy target
